s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Sin, Wrongdoing, Guilt
s.d: what a person has done in transgressing the will and law of God by some false step or failure{N:001}

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Change an Opinion Concerning Truth
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of παραρρέω ‘to flow from alongside,’ not occurring in the NT) to gradually give up one’s belief in the truth
s.g: to give up a belief; to drift away from a belief
s.c: It is also possible to render μήποτε παραρυῶμεν in ⟦Hebrews 2:1|Hebrews 2:1⟧ as ‘so that we will not gradually give up believing what we have believed in the past.’

s.dp: Communication › Non-Verbal Communication
s.d: pertaining to being marked with a sign
s.g: having a sign of; being marked
s.c: In ⟦Acts 28:11|Acts 28:11⟧ the reference is to the images of the Dioscuri, ‘the twin gods,’ carved on the prow of the ship. For παράσημον as a noun, see παράσημος LN 6.51.

s.dp: Artifacts › Boats and Parts of Boats
s.d: an identifying emblem, possibly a carved figurehead at the prow of a ship
s.c: In translating the expression ‘emblem of the Twin Gods’ it may be possible to use a phrase such as ‘a carving of the Twin Gods’ or ‘a statue of the Twin Gods.’ For παράσημος as an adjective, see LN 33.479.

s.dp: Household Activities
s.d: to prepare or cook a meal
s.g: to prepare a meal; to get a meal ready

s.dp: Ready, Prepared
s.d: to be or to become ready for some purpose
s.g: to be ready; to make ready; to become ready; to prepare

s.dp: Time › Units of Time with Reference to Other Units or Points of Time: Yesterday, Today, Next Day
s.d: a day on which preparations were made for a sacred or feast day
s.c: The identification of παρασκευή with Friday became so traditional that it eventually came to be the present-day Greek term for ‘Friday.’

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time with Reference to Some Point of Time: Until, Delay, Still, From
s.d: to extend a period of time
s.c: For another interpretation of παρατείνω in ⟦Acts 20:7|Acts 20:7⟧, see LN 68.21.

s.dp: Aspect › Continue
s.d: to cause an event to continue beyond an expected period of time

s.d: to watch closely or diligently

s.d: to keep or maintain a tradition or custom

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › See
s.d: to watch closely or diligently

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Give
s.d: to give or to provide for, with the implication of placing something in front of a person, normally food
s.g: to give food to; to provide with food

s.dp: Communication › Discourse Types

s.g: to tell a parable; to utter a parable

s.dp: Help, Care For › Entrust To the Care Of
s.d: to entrust oneself to the care of someone
s.g: to entrust oneself to; to commit oneself to the care of

s.dp: True, False
s.d: to establish evidence to show that something is true
s.g: to show to be true; to present evidence of truth; to prove

s.dp: Existence in Space › Be in a Place
s.d: to happen to be in a place

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: pertaining to a relatively short period of time, with emphasis upon the temporary nature of the event or state
s.g: not long; temporary; for a little while; for a while

s.d: to cause to move along continually in the same direction as the force involved
s.g: to drive along; to carry along

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Change an Opinion Concerning Truth
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:παραφέρω<SDBG:παραφέρω:000000>}[a] ‘to carry along,’ {D:15.162}) to cause someone to depart from an earlier belief, with the implication of accepting a belief which is false
s.g: to mislead; to lead astray; to carry off

s.dp: Case › To Cause To Experience
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to take the cup … from) to cause someone to not undergo some trying experience
s.g: to cause someone not to experience; to take the cup from

s.dp: Think › To Think, Thought
s.d: to think or reason in a completely irrational manner{N:001}
s.g: to not be in one’s right mind; to be insane; to be mad; to be out of one’s mind; insanity; madness

s.dp: Think › To Think, Thought
s.d: to think or reason in a completely irrational manner{N:001}
s.g: to not be in one’s right mind; to be insane; to be mad; to be out of one’s mind; insanity; madness
s.c: It may be necessary in some languages to restructure the expression ‘stopped the prophet’s insane action.’ This can often be done by saying ‘prevented the prophet from acting like a crazy person.’ In other languages παραφρονία is best rendered by an idiomatic expression such as ‘wandering thoughts’ or ‘twisted thoughts.’

s.dp: Time › Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
s.d: to experience the winter season
s.g: to spend the winter; to be in a place during the winter

s.dp: Time › Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
s.d: experience of the winter season

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: pertaining to an extremely short period of time between a previous state or event and a subsequent state or event
s.c: In a number of contexts there is the implication of unexpectedness, but this seems to be a derivative of the context as a whole and not a part of the meaning of the lexical items.

s.dp: Animals
s.d: refers to two members of the large cat family: Panthera pardus - leopard; about 2 m in length and yellowish brown with black spots arranged in rosettes all over the body and tail; hunts by stalking prey; and Acinonyx jubatus - cheetah; spotted but are slightly smaller and have longer legs than leopards; extremely fast; symbol of violent danger or of speed (cheetah)
s.c: As in the case of the term for ‘bear’ (LN 4.12), this reference to a leopard occurs in the NT only in ⟦Revelation 13:2|Revelation 13:2⟧ and is likewise used as a means of describing the apocalyptic beast. A term referring to a local type of leopard or jaguar would be perfectly appropriate, and in some languages a term referring to a mountain lion has been employed. In other instances the equivalent expression is based upon a phrase meaning ‘fierce, large, cat-like animal.’ A borrowed term may also be employed with a descriptive classifier, for example, ‘an animal called leopard.’

s.dp: Existence in Space › Be in a Place
s.d: to be present at a particular time and place{N:001}
s.g: to be present; to be here; to be there; to be at hand

s.dp: Linear Movement › Come, Come To, Arrive
s.d: to come to be present at a particular place
s.g: to come; to arrive; to come to be present

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Have, Possess, Property, Owner
s.d: (derivative of {L:πάρειμι<SDBG:πάρειμι:000000>}[a], ‘to be present,’ {D:85.23}) what one has on hand as available for use

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: a specific time corresponding to some other time
s.g: the present; that which exists at any time

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Happen
s.d: to allow not to do

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Sickness, Disease, Weakness
s.d: to suffer weakness or disability in some part of the body
s.g: to be weak; to be weakened
s.c: In some languages ‘weak hands’ may be expressed as ‘hands that cannot hold anything’ or ‘hands that cannot do anything.’

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Happen
s.d: to cause something to happen by introducing factors from outside
s.g: to bring in; to cause from outside

s.dp: Association › Join, Begin To Associate
s.d: pertaining to joining with someone under false pretenses and motivations
s.c: It is possible that παρείσακτος in ⟦Galatians 2:4|Galatians 2:4⟧ may be interpreted as a passive in the sense of ‘induced to join.’

s.dp: Association › Join, Begin To Associate
s.d: to join surreptitiously with evil intent
s.g: to slip into a group unnoticed; to join unnoticed

s.dp: Association › Join, Begin To Associate
s.d: to join surreptitiously with evil intent
s.g: to slip into a group unnoticed; to join unnoticed

s.dp: Aspect › Do Intensely or Extensively
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to bring every effort to) to do one’s very best in attempting to do something
s.g: to do one’s best; to make every effort to; to try as hard as possible
s.c: In some languages it may be almost impossible to speak of ‘adding goodness to faith.’ However, an appropriate equivalent of this expression in ⟦2 Peter 1:5|2 Peter 1:5⟧ may be ‘do your best to be good as well as to believe.’

s.dp: Nature, Class, Example › Different Kind or Class
s.d: pertaining to being different and in addition to something else, with the implication of something being external to central concerns

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Population Centers
s.d: a temporary population center consisting of an encampment{N:001}
s.c: The equivalent of ‘camp’ in the context of ⟦Hebrews 13:11|Hebrews 13:11⟧ is often ‘a city of tents’ or ‘where people lived only for a short time.’

s.dp: Constructions › Buildings
s.d: a camp or barracks for soldiers{N:002}
s.c: In the NT παρεμβολή is used to refer to the place where Roman troops were housed in Jerusalem and to the place in Rome where soldiers who accompanied Paul were quartered. Though many languages have a set phrase or technical expression for soldiers barracks, it may be necessary in some cases to use a descriptive phrase, for example, ‘where soldiers lived or where soldiers lived together.’

s.dp: Trouble, Hardship, Relief, Favorable Circumstances › Cause Trouble, Hardship
s.d: to cause extra difficulty and hardship by continual annoyance

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Political
s.d: (derivative of {L:ἐπιδημέω<SDBG:ἐπιδημέω:000000>} ‘to live as a foreigner,’ {D:85.78}) a person who for a period of time lives in a place which is not his normal residence
s.c: In ⟦Acts 7:6|Acts 7:6⟧ the expression ‘as strangers in a foreign country’ may be rendered ‘as strangers living in a country which was not their own.’ Similarly, ‘who live as aliens’ may also be rendered as ‘who live in countries not their own’ or ‘who live with people to whose nation they do not belong.’

s.dp: Linear Movement › Pass, Cross Over, Go Through, Go Around
s.d: to move past a reference point{N:001}
s.g: to pass by; to go by

s.dp: Linear Movement › Come, Come To, Arrive
s.d: to come to be present at a particular place
s.g: to come; to arrive; to come to be present

s.dp: Guide, Discipline, Follow › Obey, Disobey
s.d: to act contrary to established custom or law, with the implication of intent
s.g: to disobey; to break the law; to transgress; disobedience; transgression
s.c: Languages differ appreciably in the way in which they speak of disobeying or transgressing a law. It is rarely possible to speak of ‘breaking a law,’ since nothing is actually done to the law in the process of transgression, but languages do employ such expressions as ‘to tramp on a law,’ ‘to ridicule a law,’ and ‘to laugh at a law.’ See also discussion at LN 36.29.

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Exist
s.d: to go out of existence
s.g: to cease to exist; to pass away; to cease

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: to mark the passage of time, with focus upon completion
s.g: to pass; to have passed; past
s.c: In ⟦Matthew 24:34|Matthew 24:34⟧ it may be important to distinguish carefully between γενεά meaning ‘people’ (LN 11.4) and γενεά meaning ‘time’ (LN 67.144), since this will undoubtedly influence the way in which the temporal reference of παρέρχομαι is represented. If one understands generation in the sense of ‘people,’ then one may translate ‘these people living now will not die until all these things happen.’

s.dp: Think › To Think About, with the Implied Purpose of Responding Appropriately
s.d: act of intentionally not regarding or being concerned about certain objects or events

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › State
s.d: to maintain a state or condition
s.g: to continue to be; to keep on being

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Happen
s.d: to cause something to happen to someone
s.c: In ⟦Luke 7:4|Luke 7:4⟧, in some languages it may be more appropriate to translate ‘he deserves this favor from you’ or ‘he deserves your help.’ See also LN 90.91.

s.dp: Case › To Cause To Experience
s.d: to cause someone to experience something, with the possible implication of a duration
s.g: to cause to; to cause to experience; to give
s.c: See also LN 13.127.

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Encouragement, Consolation
s.d: a means of providing comfort or consolation
s.c: It is also possible to understand παρηγορία in ⟦Colossians 4:11|Colossians 4:11⟧ as meaning ‘help’ (see LN 35.14).

s.dp: Help, Care For › Help
s.d: that which constitutes a means of help
s.c: It is also possible to understand παρηγορία in ⟦Colossians 4:11|Colossians 4:11⟧ as meaning ‘comfort’ (see LN 25.155).

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Sexual Relations
s.d: the state of a person who has not had sexual intercourse (in the NT referring only to females; compare {D:9.33} and {D:9.39})
s.c: See also discussion at LN 9.39.

s.dp: People › Females
s.d: a female person beyond puberty but not yet married and a virgin (though in some contexts virginity is not a focal component of meaning)
s.c: In ⟦Acts 21:9|Acts 21:9⟧ (τούτῳ δὲ ἦσαν θυγατέρες τέσσαρες παρθένοι ‘he had four virgin daughters’) the emphasis seems to be upon the fact that the daughters were not as yet married. (See LN 34.77.) Similarly, in ⟦Matthew 25:1|Matthew 25:1⟧ the ten παρθένοι are unmarried girls desirous of participating in a wedding party, and the emphasis would seem to be more upon their being unmarried rather than upon their being virgins.|In obtaining a satisfactory term for ‘virgin,’ there are often a number of difficulties. For example, a term which designates a virgin may also imply participation in a particular set of ritual or cult practices consisting of puberty rites, in which ritual sexual intercourse is an integral element. In some languages a term which technically means ‘virgin’ is also employed with unacceptable connotations in that it may suggest that the woman in question has a queer personality or unattractive appearance and therefore is to be sexually avoided. In some instances a term which in some contexts may be equivalent to ‘virgin’ may also refer to a homosexual female who has not had relations with a man but who does engage in sexual relations with women.

s.dp: People › Males
s.d: an adult male who has not engaged in sexual relations with a woman
s.c: It is very rare that the same term can be applied to a man who has not engaged in sexual relations with a woman as is used in speaking of a woman who has not had sexual relations with a man. In fact, in English the use of ‘virgin’ as applied to a man seems strange. In many languages there is simply no term for a man who is a virgin, since such a state is regarded as being rather unthinkable. However, the first part of this statement in ⟦Revelation 14:4|Revelation 14:4⟧ indicates clearly the state of the persons in question. But if one does attempt to find a satisfactory term, it is important to determine whether such a word implies homosexuality, for this tends to be the case in some languages. See also comments at LN 9.39.|In most languages terms for the age-grading of females parallel quite closely those relating to males. The principal distinctions in age include (1) girl babies before the age of weaning; (2) from weaning to puberty; (3) from puberty to marriage; (4) from marriage to menopause; and (5) after menopause.

s.dp: Association › Marriage, Divorce
s.d: a person who has not as yet married (and possibly implying virginity)
s.c: Some scholars interpret παρθένος as referring not only to those who have never married, but also to widows and widowers who have not remarried. The meaning of unmarried persons who are not necessarily virgins is well attested in Greek from classical times.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: (derivative of Παρθία ‘Parthia,’ not occurring in the NT) a person who is a native of Parthia, a region southeast of Media

s.dp: Existence in Space › Be in a Place
s.d: to cause to be in a place
s.g: to present (oneself); to cause to be

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › State
s.d: to cause something to be or to serve as
s.g: to cause to be; to cause to serve as; to make something be

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Exist
s.d: to cause to come into existence
s.g: to cause to exist; to provide; to raise up

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Give
s.d: to make something available to someone without necessarily involving actual change of ownership
s.g: to make available; to provide; to present to

s.dp: Control, Rule › Hand Over, Betray
s.d: to deliver a person into the control of someone else, involving either the handing over of a presumably guilty person for punishment by authorities or the handing over of an individual to an enemy who will presumably take undue advantage of the victim
s.g: to hand over; to turn over to; to betray
s.c: As is the case in English, a number of languages make a clear distinction between legitimate handing over of a presumably guilty person to a civil authority and the betrayal of a person in the in-group to someone in the out-group.

s.dp: True, False
s.d: to establish evidence to show that something is true
s.g: to show to be true; to present evidence of truth; to prove

s.dp: Stances and Events Related to Stances › Stand
s.d: to stand near or alongside of someone, either with friendly or hostile intent
s.c: To indicate merely that the kings of the earth were present may not be sufficient to communicate satisfactorily the hostile intent implied by the context of ⟦Acts 4:26|Acts 4:26⟧. It may therefore be important to translate ‘the kings of earth prepared themselves’ or even ‘the kings of earth armed themselves.’

s.dp: Existence in Space › Be in a Place
s.d: to be in proximity to something
s.g: to be near; to be at; to be nearby

s.dp: Existence in Space › Be in a Place
s.d: to be in front of something, presumably facing it
s.g: to be in front of; to stand before
s.c: The actual body stance in translating παρίστημι is not crucial to the meaning; the focus in ⟦Acts 27:24|Acts 27:24⟧ is simply upon the position in front of the emperor.

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: to occur at a particular or expected time
s.g: to take place; to be; to occur

s.dp: Linear Movement › Come, Come To, Arrive
s.d: to come to be present at a particular place
s.g: to come; to arrive; to come to be present

s.dp: Help, Care For › Help
s.d: to assist in supplying what may be needed{N:003}

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: one of the seven helpers in the church in Jerusalem

s.dp: Linear Movement › Pass, Cross Over, Go Through, Go Around
s.d: to pass by some point of reference as one travels
s.g: to pass by; to travel on through; to travel past
s.c: A strictly literal translation of ⟦1 Corinthians 16:7|1 Corinthians 16:7⟧ in the form ‘I do not want to see you just briefly as I travel past’ may be misleading, for it might imply that Paul simply did not want to have a glance at the people as he travelled past. In fact, the negative in this expression may result in serious misunderstanding, and therefore it may be better to translate ‘I want to have an opportunity to talk with you as I travel on through’ or ‘I wish to visit you at least for a while as I journey on.’

s.dp: Existence in Space › Dwell, Reside
s.d: to live or dwell temporari ly in a place as a stranger
s.g: to dwell temporarily; to be a foreigner

s.dp: Existence in Space › Dwell, Reside
s.d: to dwell more or less permanently in a place which is not one’s own country (compare related meanings in {D:11.7}.)
s.g: to sojourn; to live as a foreigner

s.dp: Existence in Space › Dwell, Reside
s.d: (derivative of {L:παροικέω<SDBG:παροικέω:000001>}[b] ‘to sojourn,’ {D:85.78}) the time or occasion of one’s living in a place as a foreigner

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Political
s.d: (derivative of {L:παροικέω<SDBG:παροικέω:000001>}[b] ‘to live as a foreigner,’ {D:85.78}) a person who for a period of time lives in a place which is not his normal residence
s.c: In ⟦Acts 7:6|Acts 7:6⟧ the expression ‘as strangers in a foreign country’ may be rendered ‘as strangers living in a country which was not their own.’ Similarly, ‘who live as aliens’ may also be rendered as ‘who live in countries not their own’ or ‘who live with people to whose nation they do not belong.’

s.dp: Communication › Discourse Types
s.d: a short saying in fixed form, emphasizing some general truth
s.c: In a context such as ⟦2 Peter 2:22|2 Peter 2:22⟧ one may render ‘saying’ as ‘what people so often say’ or ‘what is often said.’

s.dp: Communication › Discourse Types
s.d: a relatively short narrative with symbolic meaning
s.g: parable; figure; allegory; figure of speech
s.c: In almost all languages there is some way of speaking about parables or allegories. The equivalent in some languages may be ‘a likeness story’ or ‘a story that teaches’ or ‘a story that points the way’ or ‘words that have another meaning’ or ‘words that are saying something else important.’|Some scholars have insisted that in the NT παραβολή is used only in the sense of a story with one level of symbolic meaning, but in some contexts παραβολή is also used to identify allegories in which each element of the account has a symbolic significance. It is therefore extremely difficult to make a rigid distinction between parables and allegories.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Drunkenness
s.d: a person who habitually drinks too much and thus becomes a drunkard{N:001}

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: to mark the passage of time, with focus upon completion
s.g: to pass; to have passed; past

s.dp: Comparison
s.d: to be very much like something
s.g: to resemble closely; to be very similar to; to be just like

s.dp: Comparison
s.d: pertaining to being closely similar to
s.g: resembling closely; much alike; very similar

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Anger, Be Indignant With
s.d: to be provoked or upset at someone or something involving severe emotional concern
s.g: to be provoked; to be upset
s.c: In some languages the expression ‘to be greatly upset’ must be rendered idiomatically as ‘his heart was eating him’ or ‘his stomach was hot.’

s.dp: Case › Agent in a Causative Role Marked by Verbs
s.d: a marker of a causative relation, with the implication of stimulating a change in motivation or attitude

s.dp: Communication › Argue, Quarrel
s.d: a severe argument based on intense difference of opinion
s.g: sharp argument; sharp difference of opinion

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Anger, Be Indignant With
s.d: (derivative of {L:παροργισμός<SDBG:παροργισμός:000000>} ‘anger,’ {D:88.176}) to cause someone to become provoked or quite angry
s.g: to cause to be provoked; to make angry

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Anger, Be Indignant With
s.d: a state of being quite angry and upset at something

s.dp: Hostility, Strife › Opposition, Hostility
s.d: to stir up hostility against
s.g: to stir up; to incite to

s.dp: Existence in Space › Be in a Place
s.d: the presence of an object at a particular place
s.g: presence; being at hand; to be in person

s.dp: Linear Movement › Come, Come To, Arrive
s.d: to come to be present at a particular place{N:001}
s.g: to come; to arrive; to come to be present

s.dp: Artifacts › Containers
s.d: a relatively flat dish, probably somewhat smaller than a {L:πίναξ<SDBG:πίναξ:000000>} ({D:6.134}); made of baked clay or metal
s.c: In this one NT context in which παροψίς occurs, it seems to refer to any kind of plate or dish, though in contexts outside the NT, παροψίς is often employed to refer to a dish used for serving certain choice foods and delicacies.

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Courage, Boldness
s.d: a state of boldness and confidence, sometimes implying intimidating circumstances

s.dp: Communication › Speak, Talk
s.d: (derivative of {L:παρρησία<SDBG:παρρησία:000000>} ‘boldness,’ {D:25.158}) to speak openly about something and with complete confidence
s.g: to speak boldly; to speak openly
s.c: In some languages the equivalent of ‘to speak boldly’ is ‘to speak regardless of who is listening’ or ‘to speak without fearing’ or ‘to speak without worrying.’

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Courage, Boldness
s.d: to have courage or boldness in the face of danger or opposition
s.g: to be bold; to have courage

s.dp: Quantity › All, Any, Each, Every [Totality]
s.d: the totality of any object, mass, collective, or extension{N:001}

s.dp: Quantity › All, Any, Each, Every [Totality]
s.d: any one of a totality

s.dp: Degree › Completely, Enough [Completive Degree]
s.d: a degree of totality or completeness{N:002}

s.dp: Whole, Unite, Part, Divide › Whole
s.d: (with the definite article) pertaining to being entire or whole, with focus on the totality

s.dp: Nature, Class, Example › Class, Kind
s.d: a totality of kinds or sorts
s.g: every kind of; all sorts of

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time without Reference to Other Points of Time: Time, Occasion, Ever, Often
s.d: (an idiom, literally: through all) a number of related points of time, occurring at regular intervals

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: (an idiom, literally: through all) duration of time, either continuous or episodic, but without limits
s.c: In some languages there may be problems involved in rendering ἀεί or διὰ παντός, since there may be a basic distinction between (a) continuous activity and (b) activity which may be defined as episodic in that it regularly recurs in related episodes. For example, in ⟦2 Corinthians 6:10|2 Corinthians 6:10⟧ the fact of being glad may be related specifically to the occasions of being saddened, while in ⟦Matthew 18:10|Matthew 18:10⟧ the focus of meaning is probably upon the continuous nature of the relation.

s.dp: Festivals
s.d: the Jewish festival commemorating the deliverance of Jews from Egypt
s.c: In some languages the term πάσχα has been borrowed in one form or another, but frequently it is necessary to have some qualifying statement to identify this festival, for example, ‘a festival to celebrate the passing over of the angel’ or ‘a festival to celebrate deliverance from Egypt.’

s.dp: Festivals
s.d: a Passover meal eaten in connection with the Passover festival (see {D:51.6})

s.dp: Animals
s.d: a specially selected lamb (or a collective for all such lambs) killed and eaten during the festival commemorating the departure of Israel from Egypt
s.c: The term πάσχα (a borrowing from Hebrew) has three different meanings which refer to three different aspects of the Passover. In a context which speaks of ‘the Passover taking place’ (⟦Matthew 26:2|Matthew 26:2⟧), the meaning is the festival (LN 51.6). With a term such as ἑτοιμάζειν ‘to prepare’ (⟦Matthew 26:19|Matthew 26:19⟧), the term πάσχα means ‘the Passover meal,’ that is to say, ‘to prepare the Passover meal’ (LN 51.7). But with a term meaning ‘to kill’ or ‘to sacrifice’ (⟦Luke 22:7|Luke 22:7⟧), the meaning is ‘the Passover lamb.’ These different meanings in Greek reflect similar uses in Hebrew.|It is often impossible, however, to use a phrase such as ‘Passover lamb,’ since a literal rendering may suggest ‘a lamb that passes over’ or ‘a lamb that someone has passed over,’ either in the sense of ‘ridden over’ or ‘neglected.’ It is therefore necessary in many languages to expand the phrase ‘the Passover lamb’ to read ‘the lamb that is eaten at the Passover Festival’ or ‘the lamb associated with the Festival that celebrates the passing over.’ It may even be necessary to expand the phrase ‘passing over’ to refer specifically to the passing over of the angel of death, and in certain instances one cannot even employ a literal rendering such as ‘passing over,’ since this might mean merely ‘flying above.’ Therefore, it may be necessary to use an expression roughly equivalent to ‘passing by.’ It may, however, be better to use a short, though somewhat obscure, expression in the text and provide a full explanation in a marginal note or glossary.

s.dp: Sensory Events and States › Pain, Suffering
s.d: to suffer pain
s.g: pain; suffering; to suffer; to be in pain

s.dp: Case › Experiencer
s.d: to undergo an experience, usually difficult, and normally with the implication of physical or psychological suffering
s.c: The first statement in ⟦Galatians 3:4|Galatians 3:4⟧ is generally interpreted as referring to the valuable experiences which the Galatians had in receiving the Spirit on the basis of hearing and believing. Some scholars, however, understand πάσχω in ⟦Galatians 3:4|Galatians 3:4⟧ as referring to difficult experiences resulting from those who opposed this new faith in Jesus Christ.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a city in Lycia on the southwest coast of Asia Minor

s.dp: Physical Impact › Hit, Strike
s.d: to strike a heavy blow, implying severe damage
s.c: The context of ⟦Luke 22:50|Luke 22:50⟧ indicates that a sword was used in striking the blow.

s.dp: Violence, Harm, Destroy, Kill › Kill
s.d: to slay by means of a mortal blow or disease

s.dp: Linear Movement › Walk, Step
s.d: to step on something
s.g: to step on; to tread on
s.c: It is possible to interpret πατέω in ⟦Luke 10:19|Luke 10:19⟧ as meaning ‘to trample,’ with emphasis upon the impact of the feet upon the snakes (see LN 19.51). It is important in rendering ⟦Luke 10:19|Luke 10:19⟧ not to give the impression that someone is to merely walk on a mass of snakes; this is simply a matter of accidentally stepping on a poisonous snake or scorpion.

s.dp: Physical Impact › Press
s.d: to step down on, with the possible implication of continuous or repeated action
s.c: The occurrence of πατέω in the figurative context of ⟦Revelation 19:15|Revelation 19:15⟧ is based upon the practice of persons squeezing out the juice from grapes by trampling on the grapes in a large vat or container which had an opening at the bottom through which the grape juice could flow.

s.dp: Violence, Harm, Destroy, Kill › Harm, Wound
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:πατέω<SDBG:πατέω:000001>}[b] ‘to trample,’ {D:19.51}) to harm severely by subjugation
s.g: to trample on; to subdue by force
s.c: For another interpretation of πατέω in ⟦Luke 21:24|Luke 21:24⟧, see LN 39.54.

s.dp: Hostility, Strife › Conquer
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:πατέω<SDBG:πατέω:000001>}[b] ‘to trample,’ {D:19.51}) to conquer and keep under subjection
s.c: For another interpretation of πατέω in ⟦Luke 21:24|Luke 21:24⟧, see LN 20.22.

s.dp: Kinship Terms › Kinship Relations Involving Successive Generations
s.d: one’s biological or adoptive male parent{N:001}
s.c: In some languages it may be necessary to distinguish clearly between a term for one’s biological father and an expression which refers to one’s legal father.

s.dp: Kinship Terms › Kinship Relations Involving Successive Generations
s.d: biological or legal parents
s.c: In a number of instances it may be necessary to translate ‘parents’ as simply ‘father and mother.’

s.dp: Kinship Terms › Kinship Relations Involving Successive Generations
s.d: a person several preceding generations removed from the reference person
s.c: In a number of languages one’s forefathers may be referred to simply as ‘fathers who have long since died.’ In other languages they may be referred to as ‘fathers of other generations’ or ‘fathers of ancient times.’

s.dp: Supernatural Beings and Powers › Supernatural Beings
s.d: (title for God, literally: father) one who combines aspects of supernatural authority and care for his people{N:002}
s.c: In a number of languages it is necessary to distinguish clearly between ‘Father’ when referring to the heavenly Father and ‘father’ as a reference to a human father. The use of capitalization is quite satisfactory for the individual who is reading a text but not for one who is hearing it read, and since more people hear a text read than read it for themselves, it is essential that the reference of ‘Father’ be clear. In order to identify the use of ‘Father’ as a title for God, it is possible in many languages to use ‘Father in heaven’ or ‘Father above’ or ‘Father God.’|In some languages it may even be necessary to identify the ‘Father’ as the creator and therefore employ a phrase such as ‘our Father who created us.’|A particularly complicating factor involved in the use of ‘Father’ as a title for God is its occurrence without a pronominal reference as to whose father is involved. For example, in a number of languages one cannot speak of ‘father’ without indicating whose father, because a person does not become a father except by some relationship to another individual. Therefore, one must always speak of ‘my father’ or ‘his father’ and never simply ‘the father.’ In passages in which Jesus is speaking of ‘the Father’ in relationship to himself, it is necessary usually to employ a phrase such as ‘my Father.’ When, however, ‘Father’ is used as a title for ‘God’ in his relationship to people generally, then one may speak of ‘our Father’ (normally with an inclusive first person plural pronoun if the language in question makes a distinction between inclusive and exclusive first person plural pronoun referents).

s.dp: Status › High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
s.d: a title for a person of high rank

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Religious
s.d: a member of a well-defined socio-religious entity and representing an older age group than the so-called reference person

s.dp: Nature, Class, Example › Archetype, Corresponding Type [Antitype]
s.d: (figurative extension of meaning of {L:πατήρ<SDBG:πατήρ:000000>}[a] ‘father,’ {D:10.14}) an archetype anticipating a later reality and suggesting a derivative relationship{N:004}

s.dp: Guide, Discipline, Follow › Guide, Lead
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:πατήρ<SDBG:πατήρ:000000>}[a] ‘father,’ {D:10.14}) one who is responsible for having guided another into faith or into a particular pattern of behavior
s.g: spiritual father; leader in the faith

s.dp: Funerals and Burial
s.d: (a Semitic idiom, literally: to place with his fathers) to carry out a burial procedure

s.dp: Kinship Terms › Kinship Relations Involving Successive Generations
s.d: a person several preceding generations removed from the reference person
s.c: In a number of languages one’s forefathers may be referred to simply as ‘fathers who have long since died.’ In other languages they may be referred to as ‘fathers of other generations’ or ‘fathers of ancient times.’

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a small, rocky island in the Aegean Sea

s.dp: Kinship Terms › Kinship Relations Involving Successive Generations
s.d: persons of successive generations who are related by birth{N:001}
s.c: In biblical times the reckoning of a lineage was somewhat complex in view of certain distinctions between legal and biological relations. The focus of meaning in γένεσις, οἶκος, and πατριά is not, however, the list of ancestors, but the lineage of successively related persons to which the reference person belongs. Some scholars, however, interpret γένεσις history, LN 33.19).|In some languages a successive series of ancestors is called ‘the forefathers’ or ‘those to whom one looks back’ or ‘those who have gone ahead.’ In other languages a lineage is referred to as ‘a person’s root’ or ‘a man’s trunk’ (referring to the trunk of a tree).|In ⟦Luke 2:4|Luke 2:4⟧ there appears to be no significant difference in meaning between οἶκος and πατριά, and in some receptor languages it would be sufficient to use a single term essentially equivalent to ‘lineage.’ The two terms appear to simply reinforce their shared meaning.

s.dp: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes › Socio-Political
s.d: a relatively large unit of people who constitute a sociopolitical group, sharing a presumed biological descent (in many contexts πατριά[b] and {L:φυλή<SDBG:φυλή:000001>}[b] are very similar in meaning to {L:ἔθνος<SDBG:ἔθνος:000000>} and {L:λαός<SDBG:λαός:000000>}[a], {D:11.55})

s.dp: Kinship Terms › Kinship Relations Involving Successive Generations
s.d: a particularly noted male ancestor (either because of his role in initiating an ethnic group or groups, for example, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and the twelve sons of Jacob, or because of important exploits and accomplishments, for example, David)
s.c: The equivalent expression for patriarch in a number of languages is merely ‘important forefather’ or ‘famous forefather’ or ‘great ancestor.’

s.dp: Kinship Terms › Kinship Relations Involving Successive Generations
s.d: (derivative of {L:πατήρ<SDBG:πατήρ:000002>}[c] ‘ancestor, forefather,’ {D:10.20}) pertaining to one’s ancestors
s.g: of the ancestors; of the forefathers

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Sociopolitical Areas
s.d: the region or population center from which a person comes, that is to say, the place of one’s birth or childhood or the place from which one’s family has come
s.c: In some languages a very clear distinction is made between three different references of a term such as πατρίς: (1) the place from which one’s family has come, (2) the place where one is born, and (3) the place where one normally resides. Special care, therefore, must be exercised in translating a passage such as ⟦Mark 6:1|Mark 6:1⟧.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: a person greeted in {S:04501601400010}

s.dp: Violence, Harm, Destroy, Kill › Kill
Communication › Teach
s.d: pertaining to teaching which has been handed down from the ancestors

s.dp: Kinship Terms › Kinship Relations Involving Successive Generations
s.d: (derivative of {L:πατήρ<SDBG:πατήρ:000002>}[c] ‘ancestor, forefather,’ {D:10.20}) pertaining to one’s ancestors
s.g: of the ancestors; of the forefathers

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: an apostle of Jesus Christ whose Hebrew name was Saul

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Persons
s.d: Sergius Paulus, the governor of Cyprus

s.dp: Aspect › Cease, Stop
s.d: to cause something or someone to cease from some activity or state{N:001}
s.g: to cause to cease; to make stop

s.dp: Aspect › Cease, Stop
s.d: to cease from an activity in which one is engaged
s.c: A literal rendering of ⟦Luke 5:4|Luke 5:4⟧, however, may suggest a contradiction in some languages, since the initial clause implies a cessation of speech, while the principal clause indicates that Jesus spoke to Simon. It may be possible in some languages to use two entirely different words for speaking, one referring to speaking to a large group, and the second indicating a direct communication with a single person.

s.dp: Names of Persons and Places › Places
s.d: a city on the southwest coast of the island of Cyprus

s.dp: Understand › Lack of Capacity for Understanding
s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of παχύνομαι ‘to become thick,’ not occurring in the NT) to become unable to understand or comprehend as the result of being mentally dull or spiritually insensitive
s.g: to be unable to understand; to be mentally dull

s.dp: Artifacts › Instruments Used in Binding and Fastening
s.d: metal chains with special links prepared to go around the ankles; used to restrict the movement of a prisoner
s.c: These shackles would normally have consisted of chains with special links prepared to go around the ankles. The equivalent in some languages is simply ‘chains on the feet.’

s.dp: Features of Objects › Uneven [Rough], Level [Smooth]
s.d: pertaining to being level or flat, in contrast with what is steep or uneven

s.dp: Linear Movement › Walk, Step
s.d: to travel by foot
s.g: to go by foot; to go by land

s.dp: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products › Parts of the Body
s.d: (derivative of πεζός ‘on foot,’ not occurring in the NT) pertaining to travel by foot overland{N:001}
s.c: In some languages a more appropriate might be ‘followed him by walking.’

s.dp: Guide, Discipline, Follow › Obey, Disobey
s.d: to submit to authority or reason by obeying

s.dp: Communication › Urge, Persuade
s.d: (derivative of {L:πείθω<SDBG:πείθω:000000>}[a] ‘to persuade,’ {D:33.301}) pertaining to being able to persuade or convince

s.dp: Communication › Urge, Persuade
s.d: to convince someone to believe something and to act on the basis of what is recommended

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Trust, Rely
s.d: to believe in something or someone to the extent of placing reliance or trust in or on
s.g: to rely on; to trust in; to depend on; to have (complete) confidence in; confidence; trust
s.c: In a number of languages trust or reliance is expressed idiomatically, for example, ‘to lean one’s weight on’ or ‘to hang upon’ or ‘to place oneself in the hands of.’

s.dp: Guide, Discipline, Follow › Obey, Disobey
s.d: to submit to authority or reason by obeying

s.dp: Guide, Discipline, Follow › Follow, Be a Disciple
s.d: to be a disciple or follower of someone, in the sense of having put one’s confidence in a leader
s.g: to be a follower of; to be a disciple of

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Believe To Be True
s.d: to come to believe the certainty of something on the basis of being convinced
s.g: to be certain; to be sure; to be convinced

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Courage, Boldness
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to convince the heart) to exhibit confidence and assurance in a situation which might otherwise cause dismay or fear
s.g: to be confident; to be assured

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Eat, Drink
s.d: to be in a state of hunger, without any implications of particular contributing circumstances
s.g: to be hungry; to have hunger
s.c: Hunger is often spoken of in an idiomatic manner, for example, ‘my stomach is crying,’ ‘my throat has been cut’ (implying that one has not been able to swallow food for a long time), or ‘my stomach is a deep hole.’

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Desire Strongly
s.d: (figurative extension of meaning of {L:πεινάω<SDBG:πεινάω:000000>} ‘to hunger,’ {D:23.29}) to have a strong desire to attain some goal, with the implication of an existing lack
s.c: In ⟦Matthew 5:6|Matthew 5:6⟧ the two terms διψάω and πεινάω mutually reinforce the meaning of great desire.

s.dp: Aspect › Try, Attempt
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to take an attempt{N:001}) to attempt to do something, with the implication of not succeeding
s.c: In a number of languages expressions such as πειράζω, πειράομαι, and πεῖραν λαμβάνω may be expressed as ‘to start to do something, but not be able to’ or ‘to think that one can do something, but discover it is impossible.’

s.dp: Learn › Try To Learn
s.d: to try to learn the nature or character of someone or something by submitting such to thorough and extensive testing
s.g: to test; to examine; to put to the test; examination; testing
s.c: It is also possible to understand πειράζω and ἐκπειράζω in ⟦Matthew 16:1|Matthew 16:1⟧ and ⟦Luke 10:25|Luke 10:25⟧ as meaning ‘to try to trap’ (see LN 27.31). See also LN 88.308.

s.dp: Learn › Learn Something Against Someone
s.d: to obtain information to be used against a person by trying to cause someone to make a mistake
s.g: to try to trap; to attempt to catch in a mistake
s.c: It is also possible to interpret πειράζω and ἐκπειράζω in ⟦Matthew 16:1|Matthew 16:1⟧ and ⟦Luke 10:25|Luke 10:25⟧ as ‘the process of testing or examining’ (see LN 27.46). See also LN 88.308.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Sin, Wrongdoing, Guilt
s.d: to endeavor or attempt to cause someone to sin
s.g: to tempt; to trap; to lead into temptation; temptation
s.c: In translating expressions involving tempting or trying, it is necessary in a number of languages to indicate clearly whether or not the temptations succeeded. Therefore, it may not be sufficient in ⟦Mark 1:13|Mark 1:13⟧ to simply say ‘Satan tempted him’; in fact, in some instances it may be necessary to make the failure of the temptation quite specific, for example, ‘Satan tried to make Jesus sin, but was not successful.’

s.dp: Aspect › Try, Attempt
s.d: to attempt to do something, with the implication of not succeeding
s.c: In a number of languages expressions such as πειράζω, πειράομαι, and πεῖραν λαμβάνω may be expressed as to start to do something, but not be able to or to think that one can do something, but discover it is impossible.

s.dp: Supernatural Beings and Powers › Supernatural Beings
s.d: (a title for the Devil, literally: one who tempts) one who tempts or tries people with the intent of making them sin
s.c: A common equivalent of ὁ πειράζων is ‘one who tries to make people sin’ or ‘one who tries to cause people to sin.’

s.dp: Aspect › Try, Attempt
s.d: to attempt to do something, with the implication of not succeeding
s.c: In a number of languages expressions such as πειράζω, πειράομαι, and πεῖραν λαμβάνω may be expressed as to start to do something, but not be able to or to think that one can do something, but discover it is impossible.

s.dp: Learn › Try To Learn
s.d: act of trying to learn the nature or character of someone or something by submitting such to thorough and extensive testing
s.c: It is also possible to understand πειράζω and ἐκπειράζω in ⟦Matthew 16:1|Matthew 16:1⟧ and ⟦Luke 10:25|Luke 10:25⟧ as meaning ‘to try to trap’ (see LN 27.31). See also LN 88.308.

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Sin, Wrongdoing, Guilt
s.d: act of endeavoring or attempting to cause someone to sin

s.dp: Communication › Urge, Persuade
s.d: (derivative of {L:πείθω<SDBG:πείθω:000000>}[a] ‘to persuade,’ {D:33.301}) the means by which someone is caused to believe
s.g: that which persuades; the means of convincing
s.c: It is also possible to interpret πεισμονή in ⟦Galatians 5:8|Galatians 5:8⟧ as the actual process of persuasion, in which case πεισμονή would be classified as a nominal form corresponding to πείθω (LN 33.301). Such an interpretation would require one to render ⟦Galatians 5:8|Galatians 5:8⟧ as he who called you was not the one who persuaded you.

s.dp: Geographical Objects and Features › Bodies of Water
s.d: the relatively deep area of the sea or ocean sufficiently far from land as to be beyond the range of any protection from the seacoast
s.g: open sea; high sea; the deep; ocean
s.c: In order to designate the high sea or the ocean, it may be necessary in some instances to speak of ‘the sea far from land’ or ‘the sea out of sight of land.’ People who live near the ocean and are seafaring frequently have quite distinct terms for different conditions of the sea, whether, for example, it is stormy, moderately rough, or relatively calm. Languages may also use different terms in speaking of different areas of the sea or ocean. Note, for example, in English the use of China Sea, North Sea, Bering Sea, in contrast with Indian Ocean, Pacific Ocean, Atlantic Ocean. In English this contrast is relatively fixed, but it does reflect a gradation of size, since sea is used normally in speaking of smaller areas than is the case with ocean.

s.dp: Violence, Harm, Destroy, Kill › Kill
s.d: (derivative of πέλεκυς ‘axe,’ not occurring in the NT) to kill by beheading, normally an act of capital punishment
s.g: to cut the head off; to behead

s.dp: Number › First, Second, Third, Etc. [Ordinals]
s.d: fifth in a series involving either time, space, or set

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to cause someone to depart for a particular purpose

s.dp: Linear Movement › Carry, Bear
s.d: to cause someone to carry something to some destination
s.g: to send something; to send by someone

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to send a message, presumably by someone{N:002}
s.g: to send a message; to send word

s.dp: Case › To Cause To Experience
s.d: to cause someone to experience an event or state from outside the area of normal influences
s.g: to cause to experience; to send upon

s.dp: Agriculture
s.d: (an idiom, literally: to send a sickle) to begin to harvest a crop by cutting ripe grain with a sickle
s.g: to use a sickle; to swing a sickle; to begin to harvest
s.c: In ⟦Revelation 14:15|Revelation 14:15⟧ and ⟦Revelation 14:18|Revelation 14:18⟧ this idiom occurs in a figurative context, and therefore it may be necessary in some languages to speak of ‘harvesting’ rather than using a phrase which mentions the literal use of a sickle.

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Be Poor, Be Needy, Poverty
s.d: a person who is poor and must live sparingly, but probably not as destitute as a person spoken of as {L:πτωχός<SDBG:πτωχός:000000>}[a] ({D:57.53})

s.dp: Kinship Terms › Kinship Relations Based upon Marriage
s.d: the mother of one’s spouse
s.c: In a number of languages the semantic components of ‘mother-in-law’ must be made explicit. For example, in ⟦Mark 1:30|Mark 1:30⟧ one may translate ‘the mother-in-law of Simon’ as ‘the mother of Simon’s wife.’

s.dp: Kinship Terms › Kinship Relations Based upon Marriage
s.d: the father of one’s spouse
s.c: In a number of languages one must indicate explicitly the various components of meaning in ‘father-in-law.’ For example, πενθερός in ⟦John 18:13|John 18:13⟧ may be rendered as ‘Caiaphas had married the daughter of Annas’ or ‘the daughter of Annas had become the wife of Caiaphas.’

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Laugh, Cry, Groan
s.d: to experience sadness or grief as the result of depressing circumstances or the condition of persons
s.g: to be sad; to grieve for; to weep for; sorrow; grief
s.c: The reference in ⟦Matthew 5:4|Matthew 5:4⟧ is not to grieving or mourning for the dead but rather sadness and grief because of wickedness and oppression.

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Laugh, Cry, Groan
s.d: to experience sadness or grief as the result of depressing circumstances or the condition of persons
s.g: to be sad; to grieve for; to weep for; sorrow; grief

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Be Poor, Be Needy, Poverty
s.d: pertaining to the lack of the essential means of livelihood{N:001}

s.dp: Number › Once, Twice, Three Times, Etc. [Cardinals of Time]
s.d: five occurrences
